profile.reading:
Intergate Seattle West Building C stands at 12101 Tukwila International Boulevard in Tukwila, King County, Washington, a few blocks from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and roughly half a mile from the South 120th Place cluster of Sabey buildings that public mapping data labels Intergate.East. Building C sits on the Intergate.West side of what Sabey Data Centers now markets as a single combined campus called SDC Seattle, immediately next to Building B at 12201 Tukwila International Boulevard.

Sabey Data Centers is the data center subsidiary of Sabey Corporation, a Puget Sound commercial real estate and construction company founded in 1972 by Dave Sabey that built its early business as a major industrial and office landlord in the Seattle area through the aerospace driven growth of the 1970s and 1980s. Sabey's own company history describes its move into data centers as tracing back to a tenant vacating one of its buildings during the dot com collapse of the early 2000s, leaving the company with an empty large scale technical shell that it recognized as an opportunity in a market starting to demand purpose built computing space. Sabey formalized that pivot in 2010 by partnering with institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors to create Sabey Data Centers as a dedicated operating company, which today describes its national portfolio as more than four million square feet of mission critical space across six campuses in Washington, New York, Texas, and Virginia, with more in development. Whether the original vacated shell that started that pivot was on the Intergate.West side of the Tukwila site, where Building C sits, or on the Intergate.East side a few blocks away, was not established in this pass, since Sabey's current site describes the whole Tukwila property as one campus rather than narrating each building's individual history.

On power and scale, Sabey's own site describes SDC Seattle as a whole, meaning the combined Intergate.East and Intergate.West buildings together, as running on hydroelectric power delivered by Seattle City Light, with more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered through redundant feeds, backup generators rated at 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity, and over a million square feet of total space across the site. Sabey does not publish a figure specific to the West side of the campus alone, or to Building C individually, so no West campus only or building level IT load, utility power, or generator number is recorded here. Sabey's certifications for the SDC Seattle campus as a whole include HIPAA and HITECH alignment, PCI DSS, SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2, LEED Gold, and ISO 27001, again applied at the campus level rather than to individual buildings.

No King County Assessor parcel record, City of Tukwila building permit, or construction and occupancy date specific to Building C was identified in this pass, and no trade press coverage naming this building individually, as opposed to the SDC Seattle campus as a whole, was found either.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: WebSearch was exhausted this session (200 of 200) before this facility group, so research relied on direct WebFetch of Sabey Data Centers' own site plus this database's stored osm_tags, which supplied the confirmed 12101 Tukwila International Boulevard address for this building and 12201 for neighboring Building B. Sabey's current marketing treats the whole Tukwila property as one campus, SDC Seattle, and does not publish separate West-side or per-building capacity figures, so the campus_power_note here is a site-wide figure explicitly flagged as not broken out by East/West, kept distinct in wording from the East campus buildings' note to avoid implying a West-specific number that does not exist. This note is shared identically with sibling West Building B (osm:way/337126741). No King County Assessor or City of Tukwila permit data was accessible in this pass.
sources_tried: Sabeys own about and home pages, this sessions fresh Wikipedia check, and a datacenterHawk aggregator listing specific to this building
profile.campus_power_note: Intergate West / Tukwila International Boulevard side of the combined SDC Seattle campus. Sabey publishes no West-only or per-building capacity figure. Site-wide, per Sabey Data Centers' own site: more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered through redundant feeds, backup generators rated 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity, and over a million square feet of total space across the whole Tukwila site (both the East and West building clusters combined), not this building or the West side alone.

reading.body:
Intergate.West Building C is one structure on the SDC Seattle campus in Tukwila, which the operator publishes as 54 MW total across two sub-campuses, Intergate.East and Intergate.West combined, without breaking out capacity per building. This facility therefore contributes an unknown portion of the campus total to Washington state's published data center capacity, ranking the broader SDC Seattle campus third in the state at 54 MW, behind only two other facilities with published figures and ahead of 44 mapped facilities that publish no capacity data. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the entire 54 MW campus would accommodate roughly 1,350 racks, but the share attributable to this building alone remains undisclosed by the operator.

The building holds HIPAA, HITECH, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 certifications and LEED Gold status, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and other compliance-sensitive sectors. These certifications describe security and environmental standards rather than any specific AI capability or tenant base. The operator does not publish which tenants occupy this building or detail its actual power allocation, upgrade roadmap, or grid interconnection status.

Sabey Data Centers operates the Tukwila campus as part of a seven-campus national portfolio totaling roughly 400 MW of capacity, making SDC Seattle materially significant on the West Coast but subordinate to the largest hyperscaler data center regions. Washington state hosts only two published data center facilities outside this campus, placing the state far behind the leading AI infrastructure states. Without per-building power figures, this facility cannot be ranked within the campus or assessed for its contribution to grid constraint at the state level.
